title: Enterprise reserved capacity triage and onboarding checklist
creator: Miguel Ortega
description:
Purpose: Create a repeatable triage and onboarding checklist for enterprise requests for reserved/dedicated capacity. Goal is to standardize evaluation across SLA targets, reserved throughput commitments, GPU class selection, and autoscaling policies so Sales/CS can give consistent expectations and Engineering can scope capacity and SOWs.

Scope: Non-bug product requests coming from Sales/Customer Success that represent enterprise commitments (monthly/annual reserved GPU or throughput), SLO/SLA negotiation, and unique scaling/placement needs. Does not include ad-hoc hosted API usage or pure product feature requests unrelated to capacity contracts.

Why now: Multiple enterprise deals in Q1 raised inconsistent assumptions about throughput guarantees, GPU types (A100 vs H100 vs LLM-specialized chips), and autoscaling behavior. Lack of a common intake flow causes long negotiation cycles and rework for infra/finance.

Primary deliverables:
- A one-page intake form that Sales/CS fill for every reserved-capacity ask (fields listed below).
- A prioritization rubric (scorecard) that translates customer needs into an initial SLA tier and estimated reserved units.
- A GPU-class decision guide (performance vs cost vs availability) and fallback mapping for regions.
- Default autoscaling and burst policies for each SLA tier, plus escalation rules for exceptions.
- A short runbook for onboarding (technical delivery steps, security checklist, billing commitments, migration plan).

Intake form required fields (minimum):
- Customer name & org size
- Expected monthly token/embedding volume and 95th percentile concurrent requests
- Performance targets: p50/p95/p99 latency per request and availability SLA (99.9% / 99.95% / 99.99%)
- Usage profile: chat (streaming) | batch embeddings | reranking | mixed
- Model family & max sequence length (e.g., Llama2-70B/32k)
- Desired GPU classes & region constraints (if any)
- Data residency / compliance needs, KMS/HSM requirements
- Contract term and hard reserved throughput (tokens/min or rps)
- Expected burst pattern (minutes/hours/days)
- Business criticality and cost sensitivity

Prioritization rubric (scorecard summary):
- Customer strategic value (1-5)
- Contract size & term (1-5)
- Technical risk (1-5) 
- Compliance complexity (1-5)
- Operational burden (1-5)
Total score maps to SLA tier: 18-25 = Tier A (SLA 99.95 / dedicated high-availability pool); 12-17 = Tier B (SLA 99.9 / reserved pool with scheduled maintenance windows); <=11 = Tier C (best-effort reserved capacity, limited guarantees).

GPU class decision guide (high level):
- H100-family: default for highest throughput/lowest latency on large models and heavy retrieval workloads. Use when customer needs p95 < 500ms for generation at scale or >200k tokens/min reserved.
- A100-family: cost-effective for steady throughput and non-ultra-low latency. Use when p95 between 500ms-1.5s and reserved tokens between 50k-200k/min.
- T4/Inference-class: for inference-only, small models, and embedding-heavy workloads where cost matters more than latency.
- Fallback mapping: if preferred GPU unavailable in region, propose region relocation + cross-region routing policy or quantized model variant with graceful latency expectations.

Default autoscaling and burst policies by SLA tier:
- Tier A: hot pool with immediate burst capacity up to 2x reserved for short windows; pre-warm policy and dedicated KV-cache warming; 30-minute scale-up SLO for large increases with on-call escalation.
- Tier B: scheduled scale windows plus limited burst (1.25x reserved) with 1-hour scale SLO.
- Tier C: manual or scheduled scaling; no guaranteed burst.

Onboarding runbook highlights:
- Technical kickoff: confirm model artifact, tokenizer, sequence length, and benchmark sample prompts.
- Security review: KMS integration, network/VPC peering, RBAC roles, and audit log policy (link to checklist).
- Capacity provisioning: confirm GPU SKU, region, reserved quantity, and expected start date.
- Performance validation: run standard bench harness (link to GH job) and collect p50/p95/p99; validate against customer SLA.
- Cutover plan: DNS/routing changes, canary traffic %, rollback criteria.
- Billing & SOW: finance confirms reserved fees, overage charging, and invoice schedule.

Acceptance criteria:
- Intake form PDF + Google Form created and published to Sales/CS (link in comments).
- Scorecard implemented as a shared sheet with auto-mapped SLA tier.
- GPU decision guide added to internal Confluence page.
- Two pilot onboardings executed (one Tier A, one Tier B) with postmortem documented.
- Engineering playbook updated and a minimal GH PR template for provisioning created.

Risks & open questions:
- Availability of H100 capacity in certain regions during Q3-Q4 could force renegotiation.
- Financial model sensitivity: how to price multi-region reserved capacity and bursts.
- Security/legal: whether certain customers require on-prem Private installs instead of cloud VPCs.
